snapshots.note: Before every divergence in the timeline. This is the historical control map that the later snapshots are measured against.
Charles V's empire, the Ottoman conquest of the Mamluks and the first evangelical territories. Switzerland stays Roman: Zwingli died at Marignano in 1515.
Mühlberg and the Augsburg Interim split the Wittenberg movement into Philippists and Gnesio-Lutherans. Cranmer's council sits at Lambeth; Switzerland has reformed late and moderately.

The Cranmerian–Philippist Communion stands against Rome, the hardline Reformed and the new Gnesio-Catholics, whose union with the Utraquists in 1575 fixes their name and theology. France is at war with the Poissy framework still unratified.
The baseline of the alternate timeline: Gallican France under the Lyon primacy, a three-way Low Countries, Gnesio-Catholic Sweden, and a Western-Rite Orthodox primate at Narva.
The eve of the great war. The Gnesio-Catholic estates of Bohemia defy the Habsburgs; Neuburg's Jülich and Berg stand under Lyon; Sweden holds Narva and the Western-Rite primate by treaty.
After White Mountain: Bohemia under the Habsburgs, its moderates in union with Rome; Filaret's catechism in Russia; France leads the war against the Habsburgs.
The peace, with Lyon as a guarantor; England's war between the Reforming Crown and the Royalists.
The Royalist restoration in England; Polish toleration through the Deluge.
Pereiaslav's aftermath and the revised Russian catechism; the Cranmerian Huguenots still protected.
A Dutch dynasty in England; the Habsburg reconquest of Hungary after Karlowitz.
